gen-dafont-bloody-gf-karla: Karla has a gaping c and a stocky, deep-bodied line. Bloody hits hard with its big round bowls and a commanding snarl, while Karla stays friendly and easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-kedebideri: Heavy drama up top, soft and open below, with Bloody supplying big round bowls. But Kedebideri, with its skyward x-height and rounded, inviting letters, is the one that welcomes you in.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-khula: Bloody brings a commanding, bloody swagger with big round bowls, sitting over Khula, a sans-serif with a squat, brush-pen belly. Paragraphs would read open and unhurried, curves holding their mouths wide.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend: Lexend has outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, with strokes that never swell. Bloody is at its best big and short, where its commanding bowls can carry the weight.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-deca: Shout on top, hush below, with Bloody leading in round, commanding lowercase. Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line and lets its terminals stop short of curling back.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-mada: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its commanding swagger. Against Mada, whose curves refuse to close, the pair gets loud drama above and a towering, welcoming midzone below.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-michroma: Bloody pushes commanding, big-bowled lowercase to the front, while Michroma gives each letter a wide berth on both sides. One shouts, the other spaces out and lets the page breathe.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody a commanding, bloody swagger that fills a line in a hurry. Mochiy Pop One keeps a single stroke width, large-eyed and neat.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-montserrat-underlin: Loud, round and unapologetic, Bloody leads with commanding lowercase bowls. Montserrat Underline keeps round bowls whose walls never swell, with lowercase that looks oversized beside its own capitals.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-mozilla-headline: Bloody takes the commanding role, with big round bowls that look best given plenty of room. And Mozilla Headline, a sans-serif with big-bodied lowercase and a splayed c terminal, can sit at a friendlier size.
